title: Khufu cartouche allegedly painted by Vyse

tellings.quote: This is like this 1800's explorer. I forgot his name like Voss or Vas something. And he was hired by uh the British Museum. He was running out of funding. He was running out of time. Lo and behold, he suddenly finds the signatures of Kufu written in very suspicious ochre.

plain: The claim is that the painted name of the pharaoh Khufu inside the Great Pyramid of Giza, the mark that ties the pyramid to him, was put there in the 1830s by the explorer who found it. A researcher named Jay Anderson tells Michels this without naming a source. He can't quite recall the man's name (the story points to Howard Vyse) but says he was a 19th-century explorer hired by the British Museum, short of money and short of time, who then 'suddenly finds the signatures of Khufu written in very suspicious ochre', which would mean the pyramid's best-known label could be a forgery.
